title: Exactly fifty
prompt: A complete story in exactly 50 words. Title not included.

title: You
prompt: Write a scene in the second person. 'You' is the protagonist, and the reader should feel accused.

title: All dialogue
prompt: Write a scene entirely in dialogue. No tags, no action. The reader must always know who's speaking.

title: No abstractions, first paragraph
prompt: An essay opening whose first paragraph contains no abstract nouns: no 'freedom', 'learning', 'society', 'experience'. Only things you could photograph.

title: Six words
prompt: Ten six-word stories, one per line. Each must imply a before and an after.

title: One sentence
prompt: A scene of at least 150 words in a single sentence. Control the breath: commas, semicolons, dashes, but only one full stop.

title: Nothing over ten
prompt: An argument in which no sentence exceeds ten words. It must still have a turn.

title: Without E
prompt: Describe your morning without using the letter E. Notice what the constraint forces you to see.

title: Unsent letter
prompt: A letter to someone you'll never send it to. Don't name the reason you won't send it.

title: List story
prompt: A story told as a list (a packing list, a to-do list, an inventory). The plot is in the gaps between items.

title: Backwards
prompt: Tell a short event in reverse chronological order, paragraph by paragraph, so the cause arrives last.

title: Hundred-word essay
prompt: An essay with a claim, evidence, a concession and a turn in exactly 100 words.

title: No 'to be'
prompt: A paragraph explaining something you know well with no form of 'to be' (is, are, was, were, be, been, being).

title: Object narrator
prompt: A scene narrated by an object in the room that has watched these people for years.

title: Only questions
prompt: A paragraph made entirely of questions that nonetheless makes an argument.

title: One beat
prompt: A paragraph about grief, or joy, in words of one syllable only.
